# Test fixtures

PDFs used to verify and regression-test the analysis pipeline.

**Rules**
- Do **not** commit copyrighted papers. Use open-access papers (arXiv, PLOS, etc.) you are allowed to
  redistribute, or synthetic PDFs. For papers you are not allowed to redistribute, keep them locally and
  git-ignore them.
- Keep files small (aim for < 2 MB each; < 20 pages). Do not commit large PDFs.

## Directories

| Directory | Put here | Used to test |
|---|---|---|
| `digital/` | Normal text-based PDFs (selectable text), single column, with numbered sections (Abstract, 1. Introduction, ...), at least one ruled or aligned table, a few figures with captions. Optionally one paper with equations. | The V1 happy path: text extraction, keywords, summary, section "flow", table heuristic. |
| `scanned/` | PDFs with **no text layer**: pages that are only images (scan of a printed paper, or "print to image" output). | Scanned-PDF failure today; OCR from Phase 4 onward. |
| `multicolumn/` | Two-column journal/conference-style papers (IEEE/ACM/arXiv two-column). Ideally also one with a figure spanning both columns. | Reading-order problems today; layout/reading-order from Phase 3 and 8 onward. |

## Synthetic fixtures included

Generated by `make_synthetic_fixtures.py` (standard library only, original text, a few KB each):

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `digital/synthetic_digital.pdf` | 2 pages, headings `Abstract`, `1.`-`5.`, one 4x4 table with positioned cells and a caption |
| `multicolumn/synthetic_two_column.pdf` | 1 page, two columns tagged `LEFT-n` / `RIGHT-n` so reading order is easy to check |
| `scanned/synthetic_scanned.pdf` | 1 page containing only a bitmap image, no text layer |

Regenerate with `python tests/fixtures/make_synthetic_fixtures.py`.

Generated by `make_ocr_fixtures.py` (needs PyMuPDF) for Phase 4:

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `scanned/synthetic_scanned_text.pdf` | `digital/synthetic_digital.pdf` with each page turned into one grayscale bitmap (150 DPI): the same content without a text layer, so OCR output can be compared with the native text of the original |
| `mixed/synthetic_mixed.pdf` | 1 page: native heading and two native paragraphs, and between them one paragraph that exists only as an embedded bitmap |
| `mixed/synthetic_mixed.json` | The known text of that page and the position of the bitmap paragraph |

Regenerate with `python tests/fixtures/make_ocr_fixtures.py` (after the digital fixture).

Generated by `make_table_fixtures.py` (needs PyMuPDF) for Phase 5:

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `tables/synthetic_tables.pdf` | 3 pages of native text with one table each: a ruled 4x4 table with the caption above; a 7x4 numeric results table without any lines, caption below; a ruled 5x4 table with a header cell merged over two columns |
| `tables/synthetic_tables_scanned.pdf` | The same pages as grayscale bitmaps (150 DPI), no text layer |
| `tables/synthetic_tables.json` | Ground truth of every table: grid, header rows, merged cells, caption, position |

Regenerate with `python tests/fixtures/make_table_fixtures.py`.

These synthetic files are only for pipeline plumbing and defect reproduction. They are not a substitute
for real papers: add real (redistributable) papers to each directory before judging extraction quality.
